methods.label: Check the domain and factor the sum of cubes
methods.explanation:
The reciprocal requires \(a\ne0\). There is a domain issue: for every nonzero real \(a\),
\[
\left(a+\frac1a\right)^2
=\left(a-\frac1a\right)^2+4\ge4.
\]
Consequently, no real \(a\) satisfies the stated value \(3\).

If complex values of \(a\) are allowed, the premise is consistent. For example, let \(i^2=-1\) and take \(a=(\sqrt3+i)/2\). Its reciprocal is \((\sqrt3-i)/2\), since their product is \((3+1)/4=1\), and their sum is \(\sqrt3\).

Under this complex-number interpretation, the sum-of-cubes identity evaluates the expression without finding the individual solutions. Since \(a\cdot(1/a)=1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^3+\frac1{a^3}
&=\left(a+\frac1a\right)
  \left(a^2-1+\frac1{a^2}\right)\\
&=\left(a+\frac1a\right)
  \left[\left(a+\frac1a\right)^2-3\right]\\
&=\left(a+\frac1a\right)(3-3)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the conditional algebraic answer is \(\boxed{0}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). With a real-number domain, there is no admissible \(a\).
